newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Omnicom acquisition to add to EPS.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Omnicom acquisition to add to EPS.

text.p: Omnicom Group Inc's pending acquisition of St. Louis-based Fleishman-Hillard Inc will immediately add to earnings, Omnicom's president and chief executive officer told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"It won't dilute earnings. Rather, it will be additive as soon as the transaction is completed," John Wren said.
The chief executive declined to put a value on the stock and cash deal, which is expected to be completed within six months.
Industry sources have estimated the value of the acquisition in a range of $85 million to $100 million.

New York-based Omnicom, a holding company for advertising agencies and public relations firms, plans to merge Fleishman-Hillard, an employee-owned public relations firm, with Porter Novelli International. Wren said the resulting entity would have $300 million in sales in 1997.
In 1996, Porter Novelli had sales of $121 million and Fleishman had $107 million. Both have shown more than 20 percent annual growth during the past several years, Wren said.

Dean Witter Reynolds analyst James Dougherty said the pending acquisition was a good fit with Omnicom's growth strategy. "Omnicom in the last five years has acquired about one-third of its growth each year," he said.
Among its most recent acquisitions, Omnicom bought Ketchum Communications last year.
Wren told Reuters that Omnicom was exploring other acquisition possibilities. "But we are very careful when we do that. We're only interested in leading brands," he said.

Wren said the two operations Omnicom planned to combine were complementary, with Porter Novelli focusing on health-care, food and entertainment, while Fleishman specialized in corporate, financial and public affairs.

"Increasingly, PR is becoming a worldwide business," Wren said. "One of the reasons for putting together such a powerful group is that it will make it easier for us to expand around the world." Last year, Porter Novelli had about $40 million in overseas revenue and Fleishman slightly less than $20 million.

Wren said a new name for the combined Porter Novelli-Fleishman-Hillard entity was yet to be determined. He said Omnicom would take months "to create a format responsive to clients' and employees' needs. We're not going to follow the format of just jamming two companies together."
